title: Convert a Number to Hexadecimal
summary: Given a 32-bit integer, return its hexadecimal representation as a lowercase string without leading zeros, except for the zero itself.
statement: Given a 32-bit integer, return its hexadecimal representation as a lowercase string without leading zeros, except for the zero itself. Use two’s complement for negative numbers and do not use built-in library methods.
constraints: Use lowercase hexadecimal without leading zeros; negatives use 32-bit two’s complement.
reference_solution:
def integer_to_hex(num):
 if num==0:return '0'
 num&=0xffffffff;digits='0123456789abcdef';answer=''
 while num:answer=digits[num&15]+answer;num>>=4
 return answer
hints: Mask the integer to its low 32 bits.
Repeatedly take the low four bits, map them to one hex digit, and shift right.
Handle zero separately; reverse or prepend the collected digits.
Each hexadecimal digit represents exactly four bits, so eight groups cover every 32-bit value.
editorial: Each hexadecimal digit represents exactly four bits, so eight groups cover every 32-bit value.

tests.explanation: Twenty-six is one group of 1 and one group of 10, written 1a.
All 32 bits are one, producing ffffffff.
